A Must-repeat Affordable Luxury
Feb 2025 • Couples
A Parisian sidewalk café in the heart of Old Hanoi serves French-Vietnamese fusion cuisine at its legendary best. The service is matched by the iconic Charlie Chaplain famous since his honeymoon here in 1936. Enjoy the most relaxing setting in Hanoi, drinks, and dinner. This is a must-repeat affordable luxury.
Insider tip:
This first-come, first-served. then linger means if you need to wait for a table, head inside to the Bamboo Bar or Le Club Bar.

A little French flair
Nov 2022 • Friends
This cafe is situated on what must be the cleanest pavement in all of Hanoi. It’s even too sanitised to be Parisienne-like. We were told they don’t take reservations and walked away disappointed but with the dearth of cafes in the vicinity we walked passed minutes later and lo and behold, there was a table for 7!
The menu is quite limited. My crab salad turned out looking like canapé but it was quite nice nonetheless. The bread basket was excellent, comprising various types of bread, and they were quickly devoured. Herbed butter was served on a glass tower - a nice touch. No complaints from my lunch companions regarding their food. Whilst the food was not spectacular, it passed muster. Service was poor and the staff seemed overwhelmed by the full house. 
We ordered the egg coffee and the waiter revealed it’s laced with a dash of vodka. It was my first egg coffee and I loved it. A lunch companion commented there’s a slight acidic aftertaste (which I didn’t discern) compared to 2 other well known versions she’s tried.
We realised subsequently, many VIPs patronised this cafe, after observing police clearing the road for a car to pick up 2 immaculately dressed ladies at our next table. Then it hit me the black suited man hovering near our table was the bodyguard and not hotel staff! Subsequently, some soldiers came to sweep the pavement and shrubs for explosives prior to the arrival of more VIPs.
We liked chilling at this sidewalk cafe, paying the higher prices, to watch the world go by on a less vehicular congested road. It’s a respite from the frenzied pace of the Old Quarter.

Amazing food and location, slightly spoilt by and over chatty waitress!
Sep 2022 • Family
Food and setting were excellent, loved the new decor. I had the scallops and my mum had the seabass. The male waiters were excellent, top restaurant standards in terms of bringing the wine over etc. immaculately dressed. Food was sublime. The experience was only tainted slightly by an over chatty waitress at the end, who talked at us while I ate my whole dessert. I was on holiday to spend time with my mum, not for the waitress to overshare her opinion about how westerners don’t understand vietnamese culture. I was more offended when she asked me my salary!!! However this is really not the hotel or restaurants fault, however I would expect in a high end hotel for the staff to read the room better. No one minds a quick chat but not to be talked at for a whole course. However; I would recommend for the food and location, it’s as good as any high end london or international hotel.

Worst experience ever.
Dec 2019 • Solo
Worst experience ever. I generally would not write a lengthy review for restaurants, but I decided to do so because I don’t want others to waste their time and money here. This place comes highly recommended as one of the best French food in Hanoi, but the food is mediocre at best. The service is horrible. Waited like 30 mins before I finally waved someone to come take my order. Not even a glass of water to start. When the food arrive, simply put on the table without any type or explanation. Something I would expect in a low end restaurant. The taste and overall experience definitely does not justify the price. The main which suppose to have truffle which I could not taste a single bit. After a starter and main course,I have no faith in trying the dessert. If you are in Hanoi, I would highly recommend anywhere but here.
